headline: LLMs are constrained by external biomedical references for retrieval and evaluation
label: Llms For Biomedical Science
summary: Recent preprints test LLMs on protein science benchmarks and biomedical literature retrieval, emphasizing contamination-free evaluation and provenance.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these preprints is grounding LLM outputs in external biomedical references rather than open-ended generation. LiveProteinBench assesses models on 12 multimodal protein property and function tasks using a contamination-free design built on validated proteins. Queryome runs an iterative LLM agent over hybrid retrieval of 28.3M PubMed abstracts to produce evidence-grounded synthesis, while DeepGEOSearch applies schema-less LLM retrieval to rank GEO datasets by contextual alignment with natural-language queries. The PRSGPT and BioStarsGPT work instead addresses adaptation, reporting a reproducible nine-step LoRA fine-tuning pipeline on bioinformatics literature with released open QA datasets and benchmarks. What is new is attention to evaluation design and provenance; the items address distinct problems, so the shared element is methodological rather than a common biological target.
